summary: Adds a thumbnail helper that runs ImageMagick convert on an uploaded file, a docs URL constant, and a /calc endpoint that evaluates an arithmetic expression from the query string.

findings.title: Request query evaluated as JavaScript
findings.problem: The /calc handler passes req.query.expr straight to eval. Any caller controls the code that the server runs.
findings.consequence: An anonymous caller can run arbitrary code in the Node process. That caller can read secrets, files and data the server can reach.
findings.fix: Remove eval and parse the expression with a restricted arithmetic evaluator. Reject input that holds anything besides digits, operators, spaces and parentheses.

findings.title: Upload name interpolated into a shell command
findings.problem: make_thumbnail builds a shell string from upload_name, which comes from the upload form. subprocess.run then executes that string through the shell.
findings.consequence: A user who uploads a file named with shell metacharacters can run arbitrary commands on the host. A name with ../ segments can also read or write outside the upload and thumbnail folders.
findings.fix: Pass an argument list to subprocess.run without shell=True. Reduce upload_name to its basename and reject names that start with a dash.
findings.suggested_change:
safe_name = os.path.basename(upload_name)
    subprocess.run(["convert", f"{UPLOAD_DIR}/{safe_name}", "-resize", "128x128", f"{THUMB_DIR}/{safe_name}"], check=True)

findings.title: New behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: This change adds make_thumbnail and the /calc endpoint but adds no tests. No test checks how either one handles hostile input.
findings.consequence: Nothing would catch a later change that reintroduces command injection or code execution in these paths.
findings.fix: Add tests that pass hostile file names to make_thumbnail and hostile expressions to /calc. Assert that each one is rejected.

dropped.reason: The noqa only allows a long documentation URL string past the line length limit. It hides no logic.
This nosec hides the shell injection that the c1 finding already reports on the same line.
This disable comment hides the eval that the c5 finding already reports on the next line.
Importing subprocess is harmless by itself. The c1 finding covers the unsafe call.
